A.2 Structure of the Body of Knowledge

The computer engineering body of knowledge has a three-level hierarchical structure. The highest level of the
hierarchy is the knowledge area (KA), which represents a specific disciplinary subfield, not a course. Knowledge

For prospective Computer Engineering students, the ABET criteria support a broad view of engineering education. A strong engineering program is expected to develop technical problem solving, engineering design, experimentation and data analysis, teamwork, communication, ethical and professional responsibility, and continued learning. This means Computer Engineering should not be framed as only learning programming syntax. For advising, the important point is that AI capability claims require careful definitions. Passing a benchmark, producing fluent text, or generating code does not automatically mean a system has human understanding, professional responsibility, or the ability to own an engineering project. AI tools can assist with coding, explanation, search, testing ideas, and prototyping, but engineers still need to understand requirements, constraints, correctness, security, maintainability, users, and ethical consequences.

This source should be combined with labor-market and developer-trend sources when answering career questions. It should not be used alone to predict employment. Its value is in making answers less simplistic and less sensational.

Student-facing guidance: learn to use AI tools critically.
